65446103.extract:
# Cow (Mario)

Cow (Mario) refers to the recurring bovine creatures associated with farm‑themed courses in Nintendo’s Mario Kart series and, since 2025, to a named, playable character in Mario Kart World whose roster entry is “Cow.” The species first appeared visually as background cattle on the Nintendo 64 track Moo Moo Farm in Mario Kart 64 (released December 14, 1996), and later became active, on‑track obstacles on Wii’s Moo Moo Meadows. Nintendo’s 2025 developer interview explains that a humorous concept sketch of a cow driving a vehicle catalyzed the design choice to elevate former course obstacles into playable “NPC drivers,” including Cow; the character’s inclusion and visibility drew mainstream cultural coverage and sparked discrete controversies, notably an animal‑rights protest over Cow’s nose ring design and media questions about whether in‑game food items eaten by Cow contain beef. The topic is documented in official Nintendo materials and high‑quality reporting by outlets such as IGN, The New York Times, Nintendo Life, Deadline, and GeekWire .

## Definition and scope

- In pre‑2025 Mario Kart releases, Mario universe cows (often colloquially connected to “Moo Moo” course names) are shown as passive background animals (e.g., on N64 Moo Moo Farm) or as on‑track obstacles that racers must avoid (e.g., on Wii’s Moo Moo Meadows), with official Nintendo course notes explicitly calling out wandering cows on those tracks .
- In 2025’s Mario Kart World for Nintendo Switch 2, “Cow” is a proper‑name roster entry and a playable driver. Nintendo’s Ask the Developer interview details Cow’s origin within a broader design decision to make former course obstacles playable (“NPC drivers”) in the series’ new interconnected‑world format . News coverage and hands‑on previews confirm that Cow appears on the official roster labeled as “Cow” .

This article summarizes Cow’s appearances and roles, development and design history, reception and coverage, controversies, international naming, and related IP elements.

## Naming and translation

- Japanese course names associated with cows:
 - Moo Moo Farm (N64) is モーモーファーム (romanization: Mō Mō Fāmu) on Nintendo’s official Mario Kart DS Retro Shell Cup course page, which lists the N64 track by this Japanese name .
 - Moo Moo Meadows (Wii), when referenced in Mario Kart 8 materials such as Balloon Battle course listings, appears as モーモーカントリー (Mō Mō Kantorī) on Nintendo’s official Wii U site .
- In Mario Kart World’s English‑language materials, the playable character is simply listed as “Cow” in the roster; coverage uses Cow as the capitalized name .
- Nintendo and press also use “Moo Moo” within course names and brand cameos (see below), but “Moo Moo” is not the in‑game name of the playable character in World .

## Origin and first documented appearance

- Game and course: Mario Kart 64 (Nintendo 64), Moo Moo Farm (Mushroom Cup).
- Platform and release: Nintendo 64; original Japanese release December 14, 1996, confirmed by Nintendo’s Wii Virtual Console page and Nintendo’s 1996 N64 release list .
- Documentation:
 - The Mario Kart 64 manual and official pages document Moo Moo Farm as a featured course (with moles as hazards); cows appear visually as background animals on the track. Nintendo’s MK64 materials establish the course’s presence and structure, while later official and secondary sources situate cows as an established part of the farm setting .
- Credits context: Composer Kenta Nagata has stated his Mario Kart series involvement began on Mario Kart 64, per Nintendo’s interview about the audio approach in Mario Kart 7, providing documented music/credits continuity to the debut era .

## Subsequent appearances and roles

- Wii – Moo Moo Meadows (2008):
 - Nintendo’s course notes for Mario Kart 8 Deluxe identify Moo Moo Meadows as originating on Wii and emphasize that “groups of cows [are] wandering the course,” advising players to avoid them, alongside Monty Mole hazards . The original Wii product page provides release details for Mario Kart Wii (April 10, 2008, Japan) .
- Mario Kart 8 (2014) and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (2017–2023 updates):
 - Moo Moo Meadows returns as a remastered classic course on Wii U and Nintendo Switch. Official materials list the course by name within MK8D’s 48‑track lineup and indicate its Wii provenance; press materials confirm remixed classics such as Moo Moo Meadows .
- IP cameo:
 - Nintendo has highlighted a “Moo Moo Meadows” milk carton cameo in Yoshi’s Crafted World preview coverage, evidencing cross‑title branding (“Moo Moo Meadows milk carton cameo”) .
- Mario Kart World (2025):
 - The latest installment shifts to a series‑first “interconnected world” design. Ask the Developer credits a concept sketch of a cow driving as the pivot that led to promoting obstacle characters—Cow included—into playable “NPC drivers,” with an item (Kamek’s magic) that can transform racers into these NPCs temporarily. The developer interview explicitly describes the sketch, the NPC driver concept, and the world design that integrates courses and in‑between roads .
 - Nintendo’s official Mario Kart World pages and Direct summarize the expanded roster and modes, placing Cow among offbeat Mario‑universe characters. The game launched June 5, 2025 on Nintendo Switch 2 .

## Development and design history

- Developer rationale and origin sketch:
 - In Ask the Developer Vol. 18 (Part 3), Nintendo’s developers recount that while designing a ranch‑area course for Mario Kart World, a designer’s “silly sketch” of a cow driving a vehicle persuaded the team to extend the roster by elevating course‑side obstacle characters into “NPC drivers.” Art director Masaaki Ishikawa and producer Kosuke Yabuki describe this as a turning point; a quick prototype of Cow “didn’t feel out of place,” prompting the addition of other obstacle characters (e.g., Cheep Cheep, Pokey) .
- Series format shift:
 - The same interview explains how the World’s interconnected design expands racing beyond isolated circuits, folds in new systems (e.g., Yoshi’s “Dash Food” pit‑stops for outfit changes in motion), and includes an item enabling temporary transformations into NPC drivers. These contextual elements underpin Cow’s addition as aligned with broader design goals .
- Additional developer commentary and press interpretation:
 - Nintendo Life’s coverage quotes Ishikawa/Yabuki’s account of the sketch and “untapped resources” around courses leading to Cow’s inclusion as an NPC racer, contextualizing roster decisions in World .
 - Prior developer interviews also illuminate series design philosophy (e.g., Mario Kart’s sound and 60 FPS performance priorities) and long‑term contributors like Nagata, linking MK64’s debut era to later entries .

## Reception and coverage

- Mainstream coverage:
 - The New York Times profiled Cow’s abrupt rise as a viral star in Mario Kart World, highlighting fan videos and the character’s appeal beyond typical franchise leads. The piece frames Cow’s elevation from background figure to racer as emblematic of Nintendo’s playful approach and notes the developers’ public rationale .
- Games press and hands‑on previews:
 - IGN’s reporting and previews confirm Cow is a selectable, named roster character (“Cow”) and detail player reactions. IGN also documented Cow’s in‑game ability to consume burgers and steak via the “Dash Food” system during a preview session, while noting uncertainty about whether Cow receives outfit transformations like other characters .
 - A roundtable interview captured press questions about Cow’s food items; producer Kosuke Yabuki declined to clarify whether food items eaten by Cow are vegetarian alternatives, calling the answer “top secret” .
- Broader cultural commentary:
 - Coverage has included playful observations by the press and social accounts (e.g., a Japanese farmer commenting on the realism of a muddy cow backside when pastured), illustrating the character’s cross‑audience resonance and discourse about detail and humor in depiction .

## Controversies and disputed interpretations

- Nose ring design:
 - On August 14, 2025, animal‑rights organization PETA published and circulated a letter urging Nintendo to remove Cow’s brass nose ring, arguing that nose rings used in livestock contexts cause pain and symbolize control. The letter requested a redesign “so [Cow] can race freely,” and associated the imagery with real‑world cruelty. GeekWire and Deadline covered the letter in detail, quoting PETA’s arguments and noting social‑media pushback; at the time of coverage, Nintendo had not issued a public response .
- Food items and cannibalism concerns:
 - IGN’s interview with producer Yabuki captured a lighthearted but contentious fan question—whether Cow’s in‑race meals (e.g., burgers, steak kebabs) are beef or alternatives. Yabuki declined to answer (“top secret”). For due weight, outlets treated this as a tongue‑in‑cheek topic rather than a design flaw, and no official clarification has been issued .

## International naming and localization

- Course names:
 - N64 Moo Moo Farm (Japanese: モーモーファーム; Mō Mō Fāmu) is confirmed on Nintendo’s official Mario Kart DS course page listing retro tracks .
 - Wii Moo Moo Meadows (Japanese course reference within MK8 materials: モーモーカントリー; Mō Mō Kantorī) is shown on Nintendo’s MK8 Balloon Battle course listing .
- Character name:
 - The roster name in Mario Kart World’s English‑language materials is “Cow,” per official pages and IGN’s reporting .

## Legal/IP and merchandising aspects

- In‑game branding:
 - Nintendo has featured “Moo Moo Meadows” as a brand cameo (e.g., a milk carton) in official content around Yoshi’s Crafted World, indicating internal use of the Moo Moo branding across properties .
- Sponsorship/branding on courses:
 - Official Nintendo materials for MK8 Deluxe list course sponsor banners such as “1‑Up Fuel” and “Green Service” on Moo Moo Meadows, illustrating a general practice of in‑world advertising motifs; the “Moo Moo Meadows” brand cameo is documented outside MK8D as above .
- Merchandise:
 - As of the cited coverage, no dedicated, official physical merchandise for Cow is documented on Nintendo’s pages used here; coverage centers on in‑game representation and branding cameos .

## Credits and release chronology (selected)

- Mario Kart 64 (N64): Released December 14, 1996 (Japan). Developer/publisher: Nintendo. Moo Moo Farm is a featured course; background cows appear visually. Composer Kenta Nagata is a documented series contributor whose work traces back to MK64 .
- Mario Kart Wii (Wii): Released April 10, 2008 (Japan). Moo Moo Meadows introduces wandering cows as obstacles; players are advised to avoid them .
- Mario Kart 8 (Wii U; 2014) and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (Switch; 2017 and later updates): Moo Moo Meadows returns as a remastered classic; MK8 press confirms classic tracks including Moo Moo Meadows .
- Mario Kart World (Switch 2): Announced via Nintendo’s Mario Kart World Direct; launched June 5, 2025. Cow becomes a playable roster character in the new interconnected‑world format, framed by developers as part of the NPC driver concept .

## Notability

Cow’s notability arises from a documented, decades‑long presence within iconic Mario Kart courses, its explicit elevation to named, playable status in a flagship 2025 entry, and widespread coverage by major games press and mainstream outlets. Official developer interviews attribute Cow’s inclusion to a deliberate design shift, while reporting records substantial fan engagement, discussion, and a notable design controversy, all of which meet reliable‑source thresholds for encyclopedic coverage .

1.title: VC マリオカート64
1.content:
VC マリオカート64
===============
[](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/vc_mk64_01.html)
![Image 2: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)
[![Image 3: Nintendo - 任天堂ホームページへ](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/nintendo_logo.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/index.html)[![Image 4: Ｗｉｉ - Ｗｉｉトップページへ](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/wii_logo.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/index.html)
![Image 5: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)
![Image 6: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)[![Image 7: A 139x28 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/banar_vc.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/index.html)[![Image 8: A 92x17 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/banar_soft.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/index.html)![Image 9: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

![Image 10: A 620x10 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/sub_btn_haikei_01.gif)

![Image 11: A 140x30 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/btn_a_02.gif)[![Image 12: A 140x30 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/btn_b_01.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/vc_mk64_02.html)[![Image 13: A 140x30 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/btn_c_01.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/vc_mk64_03.html)[![Image 14: A 140x30 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/btn_d_01.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/vc_mk64_04.html)[![Image 15: A 140x30 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/btn_e_01.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/vc_mk64_05.html)[![Image 16: A 140x30 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/btn_f_01.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/vc_mk64_06.html)[![Image 17: A 140x30 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/btn_g_01.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/vc_mk64_07.html)

![Image 18: A 620x10 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/sub_btn_haikei.gif)

![Image 19: A 249x22 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_midasi.gif)

![Image 20: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

『スーパーマリオ』のキャラクターたちがカートに乗って競い合う『マリオカート64』は1996年12月14日に発売されました。

 コース上に置かれたさまざまなアイテムや仕掛けを駆使することで、より白熱したレースが楽しめます。![Image 21: A screenshot from Mario Kart 64 showing a character in 2nd place on the final lap surrounded by turtle shells](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_ph_a.gif)

![Image 22: A 294x21 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_komidasi_a.gif)

![Image 23: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

マリオやクッパ、ピーチにヨッシーなど、『スーパーマリオ』でおなじみのキャラクターが総出演してゲームを盛り上げます。普段は仲よしの兄弟も、今回ばかりは本気で勝負！ 夢の対決が実現します。![Image 24: The Mario Kart 64 video game has a gameplay scene on a race track with characters like Toad and Yoshi in their karts](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_ph_b.gif)

![Image 25: A 365x44 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_komidasi_b.gif)

![Image 26: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

ただ走るだけではトップを勝ちとることはできません。このゲームではどうやってライバルを出し抜くかが勝負のカギになります。パワーアップアイテムで一気に駆け抜けたり、おジャマアイテムで対戦相手を蹴落としたり……。どこでどのアイテムを使うか、どのコースを走るか、対戦相手との駆け引きを制して優勝をめざしましょう。![Image 27: The images show the gameplay of Mario Kart with different levels and strategies](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_ph_c.gif)

![Image 28: A 248x21 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_komidasi_c.gif)

![Image 29: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

「マリオGP」、「VS」、「タイムアタック」共通のコースが16種類、「バトル」専用のコースが4種類の、計20種類のコースが登場します。「マリオサーキット」や「クッパキャッスル」など、どのコースも個性的なものばかりです。また、コースにはさまざまな仕掛けや抜け道があり、走るたびに新たな攻略方法を発見できるかもしれません。
![Image 30: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

![Image 31: Mario Kart game is being played, featuring Mario in the foreground in different positions on two different tracks](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_ph_d.gif)

![Image 32: A 246x21 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_komidasi_d.gif)

![Image 33: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

ドリフトやミニターボといったテクニックを使えば、タイムを縮めることができます。![Image 34: Mario in a kart drifts around a bend on a track, a HUD showing the lap number and time](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_ph_e.gif)

![Image 35: A 327x21 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_komidasi_e.gif)

![Image 36: A 5x5 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/html_source/img_cmn/spacer.gif)

このゲームには、それぞれルールの異なる対戦モードが3つ収録されています。「マリオGP」では友だちやコンピュータと順位を競い、「VS」では友だち同士のみで戦うことができます。「バトル」ではただのレースゲームではなく、お互いの風船をわり合うちょっと変わった対戦方法も楽しめます。

 もちろん、多人数プレイだけでなく、１人でとことんやりこみたい人にぴったりのモードもあります。「タイムアタック」では、コースの最高タイムをめざし、自分の限界に挑戦しましょう。![Image 37: Two screenshots of the Mario Kart video game with text captions in Japanese, one reading Let's race to see who is faster and the other The one who breaks the opponent's balloon first wins!](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/img/page_01/01_ph_f.gif)

[![Image 38: A 157x12 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/common_data/back_a.gif)](https://www.nintendo.co.jp/wii/vc/vc_mk64/index.html)

New items, characters and courses make for gravity-defying fun in Mario Kart 8 – launching May 30th on Wii U
============================================================================================================

* * *

03/04/2014

**3rd April 2014 –** Nintendo today revealed new information on **[Mario Kart 8](https://www.nintendo.com/en-za/Games/Wii-U-games/Mario-Kart-8-765384.html "Mario Kart 8")**, the latest instalment in the fan-favourite racing series launching exclusively for **[Wii U](https://www.nintendo.com/en-za/Wii-U/Wii-U-344102.html "Wii U")** on May 30th – in stores and on Nintendo eShop. For the first time in HD, Mario Kart 8 introduces original course designs that highlight the game’s new antigravity feature, which allows players to race upside down or up vertical surfaces. Racers will also enjoy a variety of series-favourite features including the return of 12-player online competitive play*, four-player local multiplayer, hang-gliders, underwater racing and motorbikes.

New features include:
---------------------

*   **Spin Turbo:** While racing upside down or on walls, players can bump into other racers or certain course obstacles to get a speed boost. Spin Turbo fundamentally redefines the way that players compete, and makes antigravity racing even more exhilarating. 
*   **Returning characters:** In Mario Kart 8, players can race with returning characters Metal Mario, Lakitu and Shy Guy. These newly revealed returning characters join a host of previously announced favourites including all seven of Bowser’s minions, who are playable for the first time in Mario Kart history.
*   **New items:** Two new items join the fray in Mario Kart 8. First, the Piranha Plant attaches to the front of the player's kart and chomps at other characters, banana peels on the course or even shells thrown by other characters. Each time the Piranha Plant lunges forward to bite, the player receives a brief boost of speed. The second new item is the Boomerang Flower. After acquiring it, racers can throw a boomerang at opponents to stun them, and its arc allows players to strike multiple opponents with a single toss. The boomerang can be thrown three times, forward or backwards. 
*   **New courses:** Remixed classic courses make a return in Mario Kart 8 with favourites such as Moo Moo Meadows from Mario Kart Wii, Toad’s Turnpike from Mario Kart 64 and Donut Plains from Super Mario Kart, among others. The graphics and layout of these courses have been redesigned and reimagined. For example, Toad’s Turnpike now allows players to drive up certain walls in antigravity mode. The game will include 16 new courses and 16 remixed classic courses. 
*   **Live recorded music:** For the first time in the Mario Kart series, select courses in Mario Kart 8 feature music recorded by live performers. 
*   **Control scheme:** Mario Kart 8 will support a variety of control schemes including the Wii U GamePad, the Wii U Pro Controller, the Wii Wheel, and Wii Remote and Nunchuk. The game can also be played in off-TV mode using just the Wii U GamePad.

When Mario Kart 8 launches on May 30th, fans can also get their hands on the Mario Kart 8 Limited Edition software bundle, which comes complete with a Spiny Shell Collector’s Item alongside a physical copy of the game. The Mario Kart 8 Limited Edition software bundle is available to pre-order while stocks last.

To check out a selection of the new (and reimagined) features coming to Mario Kart 8, a special new trailer can be viewed **[here](https://www.nintendo.com/en-za/Games/Wii-U-games/Mario-Kart-8-765384.html "Mario Kart 8")**.

ふうせんバトル ライバルたちとカートについている風船を割り合う「ふうせんバトル」は、こちらのコースで。

*   【GC】カラカラさばく
*   【SFC】ドーナツへいや３
*   【N64】キノピオハイウェイ
*   マリオサーキット
*   キノピオハーバー
*   【GC】シャーベットランド
*   【N64】ヨッシーバレー

Play using your choice of button controls or motion controls. Attach a Joy-Con 2 controller to the Joy-Con 2 wheel accessory (sold separately) to wheely feel like you're driving.

You can also play using Nintendo Switch Joy-Con controllers connected wirelessly.

![Image 49: MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_01.webp)

With CameraPlay, you can connect a compatible USB-C camera, such as the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), to see each others' reactions while you play! CameraPlay works with everyone gathered together in the same room or over GameChat.

![Image 52: MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp)

Fire up GameChat to enjoy the feeling of close company with friends – even when you're far apart!

Talk using the console's built-in microphone or share your screen in real time. If you connect a compatible USB-C camera, like the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), you can go face-to-face over video chat.

Whether you're competing in a race or simply exploring the open road, it's like you're zooming around together!

To use online services, you must create a Nintendo Account and accept the related agreement. The Nintendo Account Privacy Policy applies. Internet connection and paid Nintendo Switch Online membership required. Mobile phone number registration required to use GameChat. Children must get approval from a parent or guardian via the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls app to use GameChat. Some online services may not be available in all countries. A compatible USB-C camera, such as the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), is required to use some game features and video chat.

Race across the continent
-------------------------

Courses are spread all across this wide world, with many different routes connecting them. Leave limits in your rear view mirror and drive them all!

![Image 61: MarioKartWorld_World_Race_Sideimg.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_World_Race_Sideimg.webp)

### All kinds of courses!

From the canyon curves of Mario Bros. Circuit, to the towering skyscrapers of Crown City and beyond. Discover these courses and more across the world!

As well as many new courses, familiar favourites from the Mario Kart series also return. Race on them all, both during the day and night!

##### Drive the routes between

Races aren't limited to just the course – they also spill out into the roads that connect one course with another. Watch out for buses, trucks, and other obstacles too!

There are five checkpoints between you and the finish line. If you're too far down the pack when you hit a checkpoint, you'll be eliminated!

…and more!

----------

Want to take a spin in even more races? Try these other ways to play: Time Trials, Battles and more!

### Time Trials

Set personal bests on any available course, or download and race against ghost data of players from around the world.

Support Features
----------------

If you're new to the Mario Kart series, added support features can help you along the way! Try using Smart Steering to stay on the course, Tilt Controls that let you use motion controls to steer, and more.

![Image 67: MarioKartWorld_Races_Support_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Races_Support_Scr_01.webp)

![Image 68: MarioKartWorld_Races_Support_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Races_Support_Scr_02.webp)![Image 69: MarioKartWorld_Races_Support_Scr_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Races_Support_Scr_03.webp)

###### [Back to Overview](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-2-games/Mario-Kart-World-2790000.html#Anchor-Overview-Modes "Mario Kart World")

##### No roads? No problem!

Ride the rivers, see the seas, drive the desert and more – you can go virtually everywhere, even to the edge of the world!

So much to discover!
--------------------

If you spot a P Switch out in the world, drive into it to start a mission! Keep a look out for hidden Coins, ? Panels and Peach Medallions too.

![Image 70: MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Discover_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Discover_Scr_01.webp)![Image 71: MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Discover_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Discover_Scr_02.webp)![Image 72: MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Discover_Scr_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Discover_Scr_03.webp)

Snap souvenir pics
------------------

Take photos whenever you'd like! Rotate the camera, strike a pose, and even add stamps and other fun effects, then share them via the [Nintendo Switch App](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Hardware/Nintendo-Switch-2/Nintendo-Switch-2-Nintendo-Switch-App-2788395.html "Nintendo Switch App") on your smart device.

![Image 73: MarioKartWorld_Roam_Scr_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Roam_Scr_03.webp)![Image 74: MarioKartWorld_Roam_Scr_04.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Roam_Scr_04.webp)![Image 75: MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Snap_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Freeroam_Snap_Scr_01.webp)

### Explore together

You can also enjoy Free Roam with friends, whether playing online or via Local Wireless Play.

Huddle up for a group photo
---------------------------

Pick a scenic spot, co-ordinate your outfits, strike poses – whatever you want to do, do it together! Talk over GameChat to organise the fun.

###### [Back to Overview](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-2-games/Mario-Kart-World-2790000.html#Anchor-Overview-FreeRoam "Mario Kart World")

##### Hit the road with your favourite combo!

Between drivers and their various outfit options, there are loads of combos to unlock and choose from!

Have a blast exploring the many different combinations of driver, outfit, and vehicle. Which will be your favourite?

![Image 76: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_01.webp)![Image 77: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_02.webp)![Image 78: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_03.webp)![Image 79: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_04.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_04.webp)![Image 80: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_05.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_05.webp)![Image 81: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_06.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Combo_Scr_06.webp)

![Image 82: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_03.webp)![Image 83: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_02.webp)![Image 84: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_01.webp)

Unlock new characters and outfits as you play. Try eating Dash Food or casting a spell with Kamek, and see what happens!

![Image 85: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_05.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_05.webp)![Image 86: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_04.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_04.webp)![Image 87: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_06.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Sideimg_06.webp)

Collect as many Coins as you can to unlock new vehicles!

![Image 88: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Scr.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Scr.webp)

![Image 89: MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Scr.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Drivers_Unlock_Scr.webp)

###### [Back to Overview](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-2-games/Mario-Kart-World-2790000.html#Anchor-Overview-Drivers "Mario Kart World")

##### Items

Use powerful items to turn the table on your opponents and aim for first place!

New Items!
----------

### Ice Flower

Use this to freeze out your rivals and send them spinning.

…plus many, many more!

Welcome to Yoshi's!
-------------------

These restaurants are found everywhere! Hit the drive-thru to pick up some Dash Food inspired by the region you're in, then eat it for a short burst of speed. Your driver's outfit might change as well!

![Image 90: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_02.webp)![Image 91: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_03.webp)![Image 92: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_04.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_04.webp)

![Image 93: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_05.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_05.webp)

![Image 94: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Scr_01.webp)![Image 95: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Arrow.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Arrow.webp)![Image 96: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Arrow_Mobile.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Arrow_Mobile.webp)![Image 97: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Scr_02.webp)

From the next race onward, you can select that outfit when you choose your driver.

![Image 98: MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_06.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Yoshis_Sideimg_06.webp)

### New techniques!

Master these tricks to leave your opponents in the dust.

### Charge Jump

Ready your ride, then release to gain some air and clear certain hazards or leap onto other parts of the course.

Rocket Start
------------

![Image 99: MarioKartWorld_Items_Technique_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Items_Technique_Scr_01.webp)

When the starting grid countdown hits 2, hold down the accelerator to race away with a boost.

###### [Back to Overview](https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Games/Nintendo-Switch-2-games/Mario-Kart-World-2790000.html#Anchor-Overview-Items "Mario Kart World")

Have a blast with friends, whether near or far
----------------------------------------------

No matter where you are, you can always share the fun of Mario Kart World with others in a variety of different ways!

![Image 100: MarioKartWorld_Play_Blast_Sideimg.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Blast_Sideimg.webp)

Local play with friends
-----------------------

Connect your Nintendo Switch 2 console to a TV using the included dock and comfortably play with up to three other players.

![Image 101: MarioKartWorld_Play_Local_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Local_Scr_01.webp)

![Image 102: MarioKartWorld_Play_Local_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Local_Scr_02.webp)

Attach a Joy-Con 2 controller to the Joy-Con 2 wheel accessory (sold separately) to wheely feel like you're driving.

Get in the game with CameraPlay
-------------------------------

Connect a compatible USB-C camera, such as the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), to place your face in the race! CameraPlay works with everyone gathered together in the same room or over GameChat.

Note: Video features require a compatible USB-C camera (sold separately).

![Image 103: MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp)![Image 104: MarioKartWorld_Play_Camera_Scr.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Camera_Scr.webp)

### Online play with rivals around the world

Race together, no matter the distance! Up to 24 players from around the world can play against each other.

![Image 105: MarioKartWorld_Play_Rivals_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Rivals_Scr_02.webp)

You can even drive around and explore together in Free Roam as you wait for the next race to start.

![Image 106: MarioKartWorld_Play_Rivals_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Rivals_Scr_01.webp)

All together, anytime, anywhere with GameChat
---------------------------------------------

Fire up GameChat to enjoy the feeling of close company with friends – even when you're far apart!

![Image 107: MarioKartWorld_Play_Chat_Scr_01.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Chat_Scr_01.webp)

Talk using the console's built-in microphone or share your screen in real time. Whether you're competing in a race or simply exploring the open road, it's like you're zooming around together!

![Image 108: MarioKartWorld_Play_Chat_Scr_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Chat_Scr_02.webp)

If you connect a compatible USB-C camera, like the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), you can go face-to-face over video chat.

![Image 109: MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Hardware_Sideimg_02.webp)![Image 110: MarioKartWorld_Play_Chat_Scr_03.webp](https://www.nintendo.com/eu/media/images/assets/nintendo_switch_2_games/mariokartworld/MarioKartWorld_Play_Chat_Scr_03.webp)

To use online services, you must create a Nintendo Account and accept the related agreement. The Nintendo Account Privacy Policy applies. Internet connection and paid Nintendo Switch Online membership required. Mobile phone number registration required to use GameChat. Children must get approval from a parent or guardian via the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls app to use GameChat. Some online services may not be available in all countries. A compatible USB-C camera, such as the Nintendo Switch 2 camera (sold separately), is required to use some game features and video chat.

12.content:
And me. I'm also the Internet.
------------------------------

I'm sorry to everyone who was in earshot of me when the [Mario Kart World](https://www.ign.com/games/mario-kart-world) trailer dropped at yesterday's Nintendo Switch 2 Direct. Because when I saw this, I screamed:

> YOU CAN PLAY AS THE FREAKING COW?!?!!!!! MARIO KART WORLD?!!!!!! [pic.twitter.com/6uIZ4A0MVF](https://t.co/6uIZ4A0MVF)
> 
> — ☆オードリーAudrey☆ (@aitaikimochi) [April 2, 2025](https://twitter.com/aitaikimochi/status/1907418898879881355?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Yes, if you somehow haven't heard/didn't notice, [Mario Kart World has gone absolutely nuts on what characters are allowed to drive motor vehicles this time around](https://www.ign.com/articles/nintendo-switch-2-exclusive-mario-kart-world-every-playable-character-and-outfit-revealed). While Super Smash Bros. has taken the path of adding characters from every Nintendo-adjacent franchise imaginable to its roster, Mario Kart has gone the other way by digging deep into Mario lore and adding every single goofy little guy you've ever seen to the line-up of kart racers. Right down to one of the cows populating Moo Moo Meadows in Mario Kart 8.

> THEY REALLY ARE ADDING ANYBODY LMAO [https://t.co/UcvrIXxg57](https://t.co/UcvrIXxg57) [pic.twitter.com/JJdofUopVe](https://t.co/JJdofUopVe)
> 
> — No Context Super Mario (@SuperMarioOOC85) [April 2, 2025](https://twitter.com/SuperMarioOOC85/status/1907442715823833568?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The Moo Moo, or just Cow as they're referred to in the official roster, is getting special attention online from the community. Already, people are drawing up fanart to celebrate this cute, goofy, seemingly random edition to a line-up that, up til now, has largely included the Mario series' most famous and beloved characters.

They're also, predictably, making all sorts of of memes:

> Mario Kart players seeing that Cow racing [pic.twitter.com/7eAN22LWPd](https://t.co/7eAN22LWPd)
> 
> — SwagKirb (@Swag\_K1RBY) [April 2, 2025](https://twitter.com/Swag_K1RBY/status/1907538841852076510?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> wanted to let everyone know that this was my first thought upon seeing the moo moo meadows cow in mario kart [pic.twitter.com/CCWZA0nqfL](https://t.co/CCWZA0nqfL)
> 
> — ticky fraggle ! (@tickyworm) [April 2, 2025](https://twitter.com/tickyworm/status/1907454600145191307?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

> The helpful lakitu when the moo moo meadow cow falls off the track in mario kart world [pic.twitter.com/7gBgLg5P1u](https://t.co/7gBgLg5P1u)
> 
> — Regice (@reg1ce) [April 2, 2025](https://twitter.com/reg1ce/status/1907504310088257664?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

The addition of Cow has also led to some... interesting speculation. For instance, in one shot in the trailer, Mario consumes a burger. Will Cow also consume a burger at some point in the game? What does this mean, philosophically, for Cow?

What's more, does this mean we'll get to see Cow wearing a variety of costumes like the other characters? Can we race as Cow in Moo Moo Meadows? How do all the other cows feel about this? How did a Cow get a driver's license anyway?

### Mario Kart World: Character Select Screens

We [just went hands-on with Mario Kart World](https://www.ign.com/articles/mario-kart-world-for-nintendo-switch-2-first-hands-on-preview) at a special Nintendo event, and yes, we did play as Cow. Cow was one of our favorite playable characters, and we're excited to find out more about some of the other unlockable weird little guys we've seen on the courses, and potential funky costumes we might eventually see Cow donning. Hopefully Cow doesn't have to eat a burger first.

We've got everything you need to know about Mario Kart World and the Nintendo Switch 2 here at IGN, from [tons of new details about both](https://www.ign.com/articles/nintendo-switch-2-72-new-game-details-mario-kart-9-the-duskbloods-and-more), to [why the hardware and games are so dang expensive](https://www.ign.com/articles/heres-why-the-nintendo-switch-2-mario-kart-world-and-everything-around-them-is-so-expensive).

_Rebekah Valentine is a senior reporter for IGN. You can find her posting on BlueSky @duckvalentine.bsky.social. Got a story tip? Send it to rvalentine@ign.com._

Meet some udderly adorable residents in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe!
============================================================

Take a drive down the winding paths of Moo Moo Meadows. Nestled in serene grasslands and dotted with spinning windmills, this course has been fittingly named for its legend-dairy moo moos.

To show our appreciation for these moojestic animals, we’ve gathered a few fun facts about the course.

![Image 15](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/DejaMoo)

**Déjà moo!**
-------------

This course first appeared in the Mario Kart™ Wii game.

![Image 16](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/SteerClear)

**Steer clear!**
----------------

There are groups of cows wandering the course. They look happy, don’t they? Try to avoid them… mostly because your kart doesn’t stand a chance against these stock-y citizens.

![Image 17](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/Mole)

**A mole other obstacle!**
--------------------------

Moo moos aren’t the only creatures to avoid. Monty Mole can slow you down with raised dirt trails and by popping up from holes.

![Image 18](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2024/meet-some-udderly-adorable-residents-in-mario-kart-8-deluxe/SignOfTheTimes)

**Sign of the times!**
----------------------

You may see in-game sponsor banners around the course, like 1-Up Fuel and Green Service.

If you’d like to purchase the game, please click on the link below. And if you’re looking for even more revved up excitement, check out the [Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass\*](https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/mario-kart-8-deluxe-booster-course-pass-70070000013723-switch/)!

This paid DLC adds eight characters, 48 courses, and 16 Mii racing suits to the game. And racers who have an active [Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack](https://www.nintendo.com/us/switch/online/nintendo-switch-online/expansion-pack/) membership\*\* will have access to all of the DLC at no additional cost!

Ask the Developer Vol. 18: Mario Kart World — Part 3
----------------------------------------------------

*   This article has been translated from the original Japanese content.
    
*   This interview was conducted before the game was released.
    

In this 18th volume of Ask the Developer, an interview series in which developers convey in their own words Nintendo's thoughts about creating products and the unusual details they hone in on, we're talking to the developers behind the [_Mario Kart™ World_](https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/mario-kart-world-switch-2/) game, a [Nintendo Switch™ 2](https://www.nintendo.com/us/gaming-systems/switch-2/features/) game that launches alongside the Nintendo Switch 2 system on Thursday, June 5.

  
Check out the rest of the interview
--------------------------------------

**  
Part 3: An interconnected world**
--------------------------------------

**You mentioned that the amount of content ended up increasing. You also drew a lot of concept art for this game.**

**Ishikawa:** The designers came up with various ideas, thinking that if the theme was a vast world, they could show things other than racing. There were sketches of characters, scenery, costumes that matched the various landscapes, characters eating... We had a vast, interconnected world in mind, so a good deal of the concept art depicted scenes of people’s lives there. We designed the costumes and vehicles as a set and created these poster-style designs.

![Image 1](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_10)

**Oh, even though it's** **_Mario Kart_****, there are some that show the characters eating food instead of driving a kart.**

**Yabuki:** The idea of showing characters eating a variety of foods came up early on in development.

**Jikumaru:** If you're traveling through a vast and diverse world, you can’t leave out the local food that's unique to each place. But actually, we did consider removing the food feature at one point. Incorporating it into the game means adding not only the food itself, but also the stores that sell it and the staff that work there, which would mean even more content.

**But you came back to this idea later?**

**Jikumaru:** Yes, while development was ongoing, about two years after the idea came up, I thought to myself, “You know what? I need food!” (Laughs) Unable to let it go, I asked the programmers to implement a hamburger model I'd created and make it so that the characters could eat it. It was well received within the team, and the designer started to churn out different kinds of food. Before we knew it, the number of variations had exploded.

**Ishikawa:** The designer in charge was really pumped up about creating them. We've incorporated lots of Mario-inspired twists and tidbits to create a wide variety of designs. I also had a lot of fun looking at those designs.

![Image 2](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_11)

**Sato**: Food is sold at “Yoshi's,” fictional drive-thru restaurants located all over the game's world. Yoshi and his friends make food inspired by each area.

**So, “Yoshi's” is a chain of drive-thrus that's expanded across the world.**

**Ishikawa**: Exactly. For example, a Yoshi's drive-thru located in a volcanic region would look like a volcano and sell piping-hot soup inspired by Bowser. (Laughs)

**Jikumaru**: As we were making these various concepts, Yabuki-san comes marching up to me and says, “When Mario eats something, he transforms.” He sounded pretty serious about it. (Laughs)

**Yabuki**: Originally, we were creating the various outfits separately from the foods. So, we wondered if we could combine those two elements.

**Oh, so the foods and outfits were unrelated at first?**

**Yabuki**: Yes, they were two completely separate elements. We discussed the idea of using coins to buy clothes from clothing stores, but that would have meant stopping at stores to shop, which would have disrupted the flow, given that this is a world where you can keep driving. That's when the idea of food came up. We thought, why don’t we have a drive-thru system where characters eat while driving, and eating makes them change outfits or transform into a different character? Though, it's utterly ridiculous. (Laughs)

**But in the world of Mario, it probably doesn't feel so strange.**

**Yabuki**: Then, the question came up: “Does Mario, in fact, eat mushrooms?” (Laughs)

**Jikumaru:** So in the midst of development, we went up to Tezuka-san (8) and asked him to confirm, “Is Mario actually eating those mushrooms?”

**(8)** _Takashi Tezuka. Executive Officer and Producer of the Planning & Development Division. Primarily involved in the development of 2D Mario games in the Super Mario Bros. series. Previously appeared in_ [_Ask the Developer Vol. 11, Super Mario Bros. Wonder._](https://www.nintendo.com/us/whatsnew/ask-the-developer-vol-11-super-mario-bros-wonder-part-1/)

**Yabuki**: That's right. And Tezuka-san answers, “Yeah, he is.”

**Everyone**: (Laughs)

**Jikumaru**: Plus, the idea of eating food from a particular region and then changing into an outfit associated with that region fits the game perfectly. As you're racing, it's a real delight to see players changing one by one into the local outfit for that area.

**Yabuki**: Not all characters have outfits that change by eating food, but some have a variety that you can pick up while driving around and eating, so we hope this will be a good incentive for players to try out different characters.

**Now that you mention it, some of the new characters in this game seem like unlikely picks. I was surprised to see Cow as one of the playable characters.**

**Yabuki**: That's right. In previous games in the series, Cow was part of the scenery or an obstacle on one of the courses. But when we were working on an early version of a course in this game set on a ranch that players can drive through, this sketch came up. (Laughs)

![Image 3](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_12_updated)

**Oh, I thought Cow was just on the back of the truck, but she's actually driving it. (Laughs)**

**Ishikawa**: Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that's when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.

![Image 4](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_13)

The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn't feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world.

**Sato**: We called these types of characters “NPC drivers.” In other words, non-player character drivers.

**Yabuki**: So it was like, “They're NPCs, but they're playable? Which is it?” (Laughs) It's pretty funny to see a four-legged Cow holding onto motorcycle handlebars with her front hooves.

**Ishikawa**: But when she jumps, she strikes a proper quadrupedal pose. So I'm pretty sure Cow is still in touch with her animal nature. (Laughs)

**Jikumaru**: It was thanks to the introduction of various “NPC drivers” that the idea to have Kamek appear as an item was born. When Kamek casts a spell, the racers are transformed into playable NPCs, so one by one they might all turn into Cow mid-race. I think it turned out to be a unique item that has never been seen before. In fact, Cow is a character who's inspired a lot of different ideas, including obstacle characters like Camel and Giraffe.

**Ishikawa**: Cow is actually a pivotal character in the _Mario Kart_ series. (Laughs)

**Asahi**: On the other hand, when previously non-playable characters like Cow become playable, it means giving them new ways to express emotion, which must have been difficult for the voice lead. We were conscious of depicting the personalities and characteristics of “NPC drivers” in a way that doesn't look inferior to classic characters like Mario. The voice team members went through a lot of trial and error in the pursuit of the ideal sound. In addition to more characters, this game also has a wider selection of vehicles for characters to drive, so it was a huge task to create engine sounds that matched the characteristics, such as the appearance and structure, of each vehicle. We tried out a lot of different sounds in our search for something ideal—we even used croaking frogs and beating drums. (Laughs)

**Sato**: There are a lot of vehicles in this game, too. Since the game is about racing around the world, we've included not only race karts, but also everyday vehicles. It must have been tough for the designers, as they had to not only design the body of the vehicle, but also consider how the tires would transform when drifting and how the vehicle would move when jumping.

**I see. Because players are driving in a vast, interconnected world, you designed vehicles that can handle a variety of driving styles and circumstances.**

**Ishikawa**: That's right. For example, the Standard Kart has a higher ride height in this game, and suspension movement has been added so that when you drive it, the tires move in accordance with the unevenness of the surface and your actions.

Since players are driving in a vast world, we wanted them to enjoy racing not only on asphalt, like on a racetrack, but also on rough, off-road surfaces. This was made possible thanks to the programmers' careful attention to the vehicle movements. We also wanted it to be fun to choose a vehicle based on the world's different locations and situations, so we tried to make the lineup as varied and distinct as possible.

**In terms of the design, in the previous game,** **_Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_****, you drove underwater, but in this game, you can drive on water, right?**

![Image 5](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Pop_Up/Popup_06)

**Sato**: Yes. Since you drive on water, we put a lot of effort into the wave graphics, too. Not just how they look—our up-and-coming programmers also implemented simulations, such as ripples spreading when something drops in the water, or waves appearing after a vehicle passes through. They made it possible to create waves on demand. This game has enemy characters that create waves when they attack, so we were able to incorporate players jumping on those waves into the gameplay.

**Jikumaru**: Racing on water is something this game has in common with the _Wave Race 64_™ (9) game.

**(9)** _Nintendo 64 software released in November 1996 in North America. Players race across the water on watercrafts at full throttle, competing for time and technique._

**Ishikawa**: That's right—when it came to the jumping action, Jikumaru-san, you were very particular about the whitecaps of the waves, right?

**Jikumaru**: Ah, you noticed that. (Laughs) If you want an exhilarating jump on a wave, you need to be able to see the crest of the wave to gauge the timing of your jump. But with regular wave visuals, it's hard to tell where the crest of the wave is. That's why I asked for white foam, or whitecaps, to be added to the crests. I was like, “Hmm, I don't see any whitecaps on the waves...” Then the programmers would say, “How about now, Jikumaru-san?” And I'd be like, “I still can't see it! Just a little more!” We went back and forth like this for a while before the job was done. The programmers really worked hard. Thanks to that, I think jumping on waves has turned into a nice little gameplay element.

![Image 6](https://assets.nintendo.com/image/upload/f_auto/q_auto/dpr_1.5/ncom/en_US/articles/2025/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-1/Inserted/Inserted_14)

**Was that also part of your commitment to user-friendliness?**

**Jikumaru**: Yes. But while we continued to work on this, the designers started to request different ways to express water, not just from a gameplay perspective, but also in terms of the visual portrayal of beaches and shoals.

**Ishikawa**: I wanted to show the shoal floor through the crystal-clear water. At first, we were worried that we wouldn't be able to show the shoal floor because it was demanding on the processor. But our programmers made improvements here and there, and we were able to make it happen. Even with the familiar Koopa Troopa Beach course, we were able to create the visuals we wanted to show... Thank you for that, Sato-san.

**Sato**: Because we were so particular about this, the designers needed to toil away to make the shoal floor visible. (Laughs) But thanks to their efforts, it improved the quality of the graphics.

**Ishikawa**: You must’ve also worked hard to create the sound you hear when driving on water, right, Asahi-san?

**Asahi**: That’s right. Unlike driving on land, when driving on water, the vehicle bobs up and down along with the movement of the water. The sound is designed to correspond to the vehicle's movement and orientation. It was created with great attention paid to even the most delicate sounds, so please listen out for it when you're driving on water.

["This Is It!" - Nintendo On Why It Added 'Cow' Into Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/this-is-it-nintendo-on-why-it-added-cow-into-mario-kart-world)
===============================================================================================================================================================================

What an udder surprise

[![Image 30: MK World - Cow 2](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.900x.jpg)](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.large.jpg "MK World - Cow 2")

_Image: Nintendo_

If you watched any of the reactions to the [Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/games/nintendo-switch-2/mario-kart-world) reveal trailer, then chances are you saw somebody loudly exclaim "you can play as a _COW?!"_.

Yes, the cow, an NPC character known for its presence in Moo Moo Meadows, is now playable in the upcoming Mario Kart tile for Switch 2. In the recent [Ask the Developer](https://www.nintendo.com/us/whatsnew/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-3/) interview over at Nintendo, Masaaki Ishikawa explained the reasoning behind Cow's inclusion.

Honestly, it seems to have simply been a case of pondering what new additions could be added after Mario Kart 8 Deluxe included so many newcomers. Here's what Ishikawa had to say:

> "Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that's when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.
> 
> 
> "The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn't feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world."

Characters such as Cow and Cheep Cheep are known as 'NPC Racers' within Nintendo, with Ishikawa joking that Cow in particular "is actually a pivotal character in the Mario Kart series".

To coincide with the information from the Ask the Developer interview, Nintendo has also released new footage from Mario Kart World showcasing Cow taking part in one of the game's missions, as shown by [TodayNews on BlueSky.](https://bsky.app/profile/today.oatmealdome.me/post/3lpousecsiy2c) The task? "Mooove" through a herd of cows, of course. Chortle!

Mario Kart World is scheduled to launch alongside the Switch 2 on **5th June 2025**. Nintendo also revealed that the game was originally in development for Switch 1, and also explained why it chose not to call the game 'Mario Kart 9'.

Roll Out With Mario and Friends Across an Interconnected World Featuring Up to 24 Drivers in Grand Prix Races, Chaotic Knockout Tours, Battle Mode, Free Roam and More
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In today’s _Mario Kart World_ Direct presentation, Nintendo unveiled footage detailing new information on the upcoming game – which is set to be the biggest _Mario Kart_ game in series history – launching exclusively for the Nintendo Switch 2 system on June 5. Additionally, a bundle that includes the Nintendo Switch 2 system and a full game download code for the _Mario Kart World_ game will also be available beginning June 5.

[_Mario Kart World_](https://www.nintendo.com/us/gaming-systems/switch-2/featured-games/mario-kart-world/) features a series-first: an interconnected world where you can drive virtually anywhere, including across cities, plains, a desert and even the ocean. Races are held throughout this world’s various regions and feature dynamic weather conditions and a day/night cycle. Start your engines and compete for first place in Grand Prix or the new Knockout Tour mode or simply experience a leisurely drive across a world of diverse locales in Free Roam. The world is your racetrack, and there’s plenty to discover – solo or with friends, locally\* or online\*\*. This is just the starting line!

*   **An Interconnected World:** Drift, draft and drive your way around an interconnected world for the first time in a _Mario Kart_ game. In _Mario Kart World,_ the game’s courses are interspersed across the world with roads leading from one to the next – so players can experience navigating roads in between courses!
    
*   **Grand Prix:** Bring home the gold in Grand Prix, which consists of four different races to win each Cup – including the Mushroom Cup, Flower Cup, Star Cup and more – held across the game’s world. And for the first time in the series, racers will need to drive from one course to the next as part of the Grand Prix! In Mushroom Cup, for example, you’ll start off racing the Mario Bros. Circuit, then the second race will have you covering the distance from Mario Bros. Circuit to Crown City. Conquer every Grand Prix Cup and you might just unlock a certain colorful course!
    
*   **Knockout Tour**: Race from one end of the world to the other in these extended rallies, with checkpoints dotted throughout. If you don’t make the cut, you’re out of the running, so buckle up for these non-stop sprints because you’ll need to keep pace to stay in the race. Your rivals aren’t the only hazards you'll need to avoid on the road, either. Vehicles that shoot Bullet Bills, Hammer Bros. attacks, and other obstacles will find their way into this mode as well. Drive to survive and keep your eyes on first place!
    
*   **Free Roam:** There is plenty to discover in _Mario Kart World_ that goes beyond racing. So when you’re not aiming for first place, take the scenic route in Free Roam! Explore panoramic vistas, go (way) off-road, see the seas and find secrets like hidden coins, or hit P Switches to take on hundreds of missions that can help improve your driving skills outside of races. You can also take in-game photos while free roaming, so take a road trip and strike a pose at the sights.
    
*   **Battle Mode**: Battle Mode is back and more hectic than ever! Secure the gold by collecting the most coins in Coin Runners or burst your rivals’ balloons with items in Balloon Battle. If you pop all of your rival’s balloons, they are out!
    
*   **New Techniques:** Leap over obstacles and more with the new Charge Jump move. Use it to jump onto rails that you can grind, dodge attacks from your rivals and even jump toward a wall to ride on it for a short time. You can also chain together wall-rides to uncover hidden routes. Miss your mark during Free Roam or single-player mode? Just use Rewind to reset your vehicle to its original position – this is a great way to undo a driving mishap, but keep in mind that your rivals will still move normally while rewinding, so try not to lose your lead!
    
*   **24 Racers:** _Mario Kart World_ features races with up to 24 participants from around the world – the most in _Mario Kart_ series history! Modes like Grand Prix and Knockout Tour allow up to 24 players to compete, filling the game world with friends and familiar faces and plenty of rivals to vie for first place.
    
*   **Fun With Everyone, Anywhere:** _Mario Kart World_ offers multiple ways to play together, locally or online. Up to four players can race split screen on the same system. The game also supports local wireless play where up to eight players (with up to two players per Nintendo Switch 2 system) can race together. And players from around the world can join a race or battle in online play. In Free Roam, you can also meet up with your crew anywhere in this game’s world. Drive around, see where your friends are on the map and warp to them instantly. Then race, battle with custom rules or take a road trip to see the sights together.
    
*   **Even More Fun with GameChat:** [GameChat](https://www.nintendo.com/us/gaming-systems/switch-2/features/gamechat/)\*\*\* features an expanded online experience in the _Mario Kart World_ game. Use the Nintendo Switch 2 built-in microphone to voice chat with friends while driving together or take a backseat and watch each other’s game screens. You can enjoy GameChat without needing a Nintendo Switch Online membership until March 31, 2026. After that, a Nintendo Switch Online membership will be required.
    
*   **CameraPlay**: If you have a Nintendo Switch 2 Camera (sold separately)\*\*\*, your face will show up beside your racer, and you can see your friends’ reactions when you play online! When playing locally with family and friends on the same system, a single camera can detect up to four people’s faces that you can see in-game as well.
    
*   **Courses**: _Mario Kart World_ has many races to enjoy across its vast world. Rule the roads on brand new courses like Mario Bros. Circuit, the modern streets of Crown City, the snowy trails of Starview Peak and the spirited Boo Cinema, just to name a few. Nostalgic courses from previous _Mario Kart_ games have also been reimagined to feel at-home within this vast, new world, offering fresh experiences on classics.
    
*   **Characters:** Get behind the wheel as familiar Mushroom Kingdom characters like Mario, Luigi, Peach and Bowser. Looking for a racer that’s a little more offbeat? Try taking Goomba, Spike and even Cow for a test drive.
    
*   **New Items**: Tear up the track with a selection of new and returning items. Throw a Coin Shell to knock rivals off course and make coins appear that gradually increase the speed of whoever collects them. Chill out the competition (and send ’em spinning) with the Ice Flower. Bring down the Hammer to nail your rival or briefly block their path. Use a Mega Mushroom to grow big and squash your rivals. Leap to new heights with the Feather. Call in Kamek’s magic to transform your rivals into something surprising and cause unexpected chaos on the course. The lower your position, the more likely you’ll receive items that could turn the tables, so when you get something good … go for it!
    
*   **Drive-Thru and Roll-Out**: Make a pit stop at Yoshi’s for a local delight: Dash Food! These to-go orders will give you a speed boost and sometimes also unlock outfits that can be donned from the character selection screen. There are plenty of dishes and outfits to find, so drive through when making your way around _Mario Kart World_.
    
*   **Even More Modes**: Whether you want to race or battle, there are even more ways to stoke some friendly competition in _Mario Kart World_. Race against the clock in Time Trials, where players can also go online to compete against ghost data from racers around the world. And you can customize the rules of the road in VS Race, where drivers can decide if they want to compete with two, three or four teams with a classic three-lap ruleset or by driving from one course to another.
    
*   **Roadside Assistance**: Looking for some options to assist you on race day? Features like Smart Steering to keep you on course, Auto-Accelerate and Tilt Controls for motion control steering are available to turn on or off whenever you like. Plus, if you have the Joy-Con 2 Wheel accessory (available as a set of two, sold separately) you can feel like you’re really driving!
    

Remember that Nintendo Switch 2 features [parental controls](https://play.nintendo.com/parents/tools-for-parents/parental-controls/) that let adults manage the content their children can access. For more information about other features, visit [https://www.nintendo.com/switch/](https://www.nintendo.com/us/switch/).

![Image 10: A cartoon cow character riding a boombox-shaped vehicle races along a track through a green countryside](https://cdn.geekwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/mariokartcow.png)

Cow, a breakout star in the new “Mario Kart World” video game, wears a nose ring that is viewed as a painful accessory by the animal rights group PETA. (Screenshot via Nintendo on YouTube)

The moos turned to boos over the depiction of a popular new video game cow character.

People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) is protesting the design of Cow, a scooter-riding farm animal in the new [“Mario Kart World”](https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/mario-kart-world-switch-2/?srsltid=AfmBOoqVlnN7ArRSV0P3qWY0Ns1On6RpJLBGA-Fzh7mg1y5oOjDkAd9M) because the character wears a nose ring.

“Nose rings are used by the meat and dairy industries to exploit, control, and even drag animals to their deaths,” PETA said in a letter (in full below) Thursday to Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa.

Nintendo of America is headquartered in Redmond, Wash.

The game launched exclusively on the new Nintendo Switch 2 game console, which [released in June](https://www.geekwire.com/2025/nintendos-switch-2-arrives-with-long-lines-in-seattle-and-beyond-for-new-video-game-console/)to much fanfare. And Cow has become a breakout star, as [The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/13/arts/mario-kart-world-cow.html) reported in July, with videos on social media showcasing the bovine’s popularity.

PETA is less enthralled — at least when it comes to the nose ring. The organization is calling for Nintendo to redesign Cow’s look, so it can “race freely — without any painful reminders of the industries that treat animals like profit-making machines.”

Read PETA’s letter to Nintendo, and watch a trailer for “Mario Kart World” below:

> Dear Mr. Furukawa:
> 
> 
> Greetings! I’m writing on behalf of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA). PETA entities have more than 10 million members and supporters globally. We _herd_ there’s a new star in Mario Kart World: Cow! She is already winning hearts everywhere—including ours. But one detail has us hitting the brakes: The brass ring in Cow’s nose.Would you please show empathy towards bovines and remove the nose ring?Here’s why this is so important:
> 
> 
> Nose rings are used by the meat and dairy industries to exploit, control, and even drag animals to their deaths. These brass rings are crudely stabbed through the sensitive septum of cows and bulls, which can cause lasting pain and discomfort. The dairy industry will also clip spiked nose rings on baby cows so that the comforting act of nursing from their mother causes her pain and the baby is rejected and kicked away. To control bulls, a chain might be fastened from the nose ring to the bull’s horn for even more pain-driven control.
> 
> 
> The brass ring in Cow’s nose glosses over real world violence and cruelty to animals. That’s why we’re asking you to give this beloved bovine a small but meaningful upgrade: Remove the nose ring and let Cow race freely—without any painful reminders of the industries that treat animals like profit-making machines.
> 
> 
> Every animal is some _one_. So leave the rings to Sonic and let Cow breathe free!

5.   **Inside the PETA Mario Kart World Controversy With Nintendo**

Inside the PETA Mario Kart World Controversy With Nintendo
==========================================================

Share Share on Facebook Post Share on X Share Share on LinkedIn

Published August 15, 2025 by [Ryan Hajek](https://www.peta.org/news/author/ryan-hajek/). 

 3 min read
The **PETA Mario Kart World** controversy erupted online after we urged Nintendo to remove the nose ring from a new character named Cow in the videogame. Cow’s nose ring in Nintendo’s game **glosses over _real-world_ cruelty to animals**. [In the meat and dairy industries](https://www.peta.org/issues/animals-used-for-food/factory-farming/cows/dairy-industry/),**a nose ring is a tool of cruelty that causes pain and discomfort—**no cow in the _real world_ who is forced to wear a nose ring would ever sport Cow’s goofy grin in Nintendo’s game.

![Image 4: social media post about peta mario kart controversy](https://www.peta.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/peta-mario-kart-world-cow-post-602x753.jpg)
In a letter to Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa on August 14, PETA’s Senior Vice President of Marketing Engagement Joel Bartlett explained that **nose rings are forcibly pierced through one of the most sensitive parts of a cow’s body**.

> _“The brass ring in Cow’s nose glosses over real-world violence,”_ Bartlett’s letter reads. _“Let Cow race freely—without reminders of the industries that treat animals like machines.”_

![Image 5: cow, dairy, nose, ring](blob:http://localhost/25d49148f3d3003311839e1625a5df6d)
**PETA’s Problem With Cow’s Nose Ring in _Mario Kart World_**
-------------------------------------------------------------

In the real world, **nose rings are used by the meat and dairy industries to exploit, control, and even drag**cows and bulls to their deaths. Workers **crudely stab these brass rings through the sensitive septums of cows and bulls**, which can cause lasting pain and discomfort.

We know Mario Kart World is just a game—and that’s exactly why Cow’s nose ring needs to go. Mario Kart is supposed to be a fun escape, not a reminder of the painful tools used on cows in the meat and dairy industries. No one wants to think about animal suffering while zipping around a race track.

The **[dairy industry](https://www.peta.org/features/dairy-industry-cruelty/) will also clip spiked nose rings on baby cows** so that the comforting act of nursing from their mother causes her pain and the baby is rejected and kicked away. To control bulls, **a chain might be fastened from the nose ring to the bull’s horn** for even more pain-driven control.

[Images the dairy industry doesn’t want you to see _→_](https://www.peta.org/features/dairy-industry-cruelty/)

**PETA brings animal exploitation to the world’s attention anywhere it happens, whether in the real world or the video game world.**

*   **[PETA called out Nintendo’s _Animal Crossing: New Horizons_](https://www.peta.org/features/animal-crossing-new-horizons-vegan/)**for encouraging abusive behavior toward fish and insects, where players can tear wildlife out of their homes and display them in cramped cases in a museum.
*   [**PETA asked for vegan updates to _Palworld_**](https://www.peta.org/news/palworld-vegan-update/), where players beat and capture wild Pals and exploit them for food and clothing.
*   [**PETA challenged the makers of Hunting Simulator 2**](https://www.peta.org/news/peta-frances-letter-to-nacon/) to trade guns for cameras and make it a wildlife photography competition instead of a game that glamorizes animal murder.

**When video games are unfriendly to animals, PETA also creates animal-friendly versions:**

*   **Pokémon Black and Blue:**While cruel trainers abuse and exploit Pokémon in Nintendo’s games, players get to free Pikachu and his Pokémon friends as they struggle for liberation in [**PETA’s _Pokémon Black and Blue_**](https://games.peta.org/pokemon-black-and-white-parody/)_._
*   **Mario Kills Tanooki:**Mario wears the skin of Tanooki as a “suit” in Mario games, which sends a message that it’s OK to wear fur, but in real life, tanuki are raccoon dogs who are skinned alive for their fur. In [**PETA’s _Super Tanooki Skin 2D_**](https://games.peta.org/mario-kills-tanooki/), players can help Tanooki reclaim his fur.

[Help PETA Tell Nintendo to Give Cow a Compassionate Glow-Up _→_](https://action.peta2.com/page/86849/petition/1)
